summary: Two sibling clauses in the same information sheet give conflicting procedural treatment to the identical conduct (a tenant assigning or subletting contrary to the lease), without ever flagging the overlap to the reader.

summary: The clause's body states the CCPA 'business' revenue threshold as a flat $25,000,000, but that figure has been administratively adjusted upward to $26,625,000 effective January 1, 2025 (and remains in force through the end of 2026), so a company with revenue between those two figures is incorrectly described by the body as a covered 'business.'
evidence: Clause body: 'meets at least one of three thresholds: annual gross revenue above $25,000,000, annually buying, selling, or sharing the personal information of 100,000 or more consumers or households, or deriving 50% or more of annual revenue from selling or sharing personal information.' Contrast with the CPPA's own published table at cppa.ca.gov/regulations/cpi_adjustment.html: 'Civil Code § 1798.140(d)(1)(A): Annual gross revenue amount within the definition of "business" ... Updated 2025 Amount $26,625,000 ... Previous Amount $25,000,000' (effective 1/1/2025; posted 12/17/2024). The statutory text itself, quoted correctly in the clause's own citation, flags this: 'had annual gross revenues in excess of twenty-five million dollars ($25,000,000) in the preceding calendar year, as adjusted pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 1798.199.95' -- but the body drops the adjustment caveat and states the stale base figure as if it were still the operative number, even though the adjustment (required every odd-numbered year by Civ. Code § 1798.199.95(d)) had already taken effect well before this clause's own checkedDate of 2026-09-02.
suggestedFix: Revise the revenue threshold language to: 'annual gross revenue above a statutory threshold that began at $25,000,000 and is adjusted for inflation by the California Privacy Protection Agency every odd-numbered year under Civil Code § 1798.199.95(d) -- $26,625,000 effective January 1, 2025 through the next adjustment on January 1, 2027 -- so the current dollar figure should be confirmed against the agency's published table rather than assumed to be $25,000,000.'
